doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Walking to Attucks and growing up in a self-contained black community
summary: Segregated schools and movies, a childhood relatively insulated from racism, in a community around Attucks and Lockefield Gardens.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: And it's interesting to realize that J.J. and them had to go across town, 'cause Douglas Park was my neighborhood. That's out at 25th and Martindale. Fact is, I was going to ask you, man. I guess Crispus Attucks [High School] became a school in 1938, 1935 – somewhere around there when they built that school. [Crispus Attucks High School opened in 1927.]

What did they do? Provide tickets for you guys to come across on the bus? Were you bused to school? I can’t remember whether it was that you walked to school, 'cause you were coming from clear out from the . . .
We walked. I walked from the north side to Crispus Attucks every day. That was a long walk, but it was a piece of cake for some reason. We walked to school.
I didn’t remember what happened when they first segregated the schools.

You know, it's interesting that I don’t have a vivid recollection of [that]. I certainly don’t have an accurate recollection of the racism that was rampant in Indianapolis during my early childhood years. It was rampant, but what it means is I didn’t have much traffic to come into contact with the horror of racism. I don’t know why I was so insulated from it, because we lived on the north side. I walked to school every day. We went to the movies – a segregated movie – on occasion, but I don’t remember many situations of violence on the racial situation. Indianapolis was certainly, and Indiana was certainly segregated for sure and racism was rampant, but I don’t recall personally having any traffic with incidents of violence or blatant hostile acts towards me or my family. I just don’t. Yet I know all this went on. We all know it went on, for sure. I just didn’t come into contact with it very much.
'Cause I guess the whole world, too, was in that area where you lived and the area from Crispus Attucks down to Lockefield Gardens . . .
. . . so you didn't have a lot of exposure, I guess, to white people, period.
This is true. This is very true. We were a self-contained community.
